question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

 

A. Two astronomers – Johannes Kepler from Germany and Galileo from Italy – supported the Copernican theory after nearly a century passed by.

B. Copernicus’ view was that the sun was stationary and the earth and the planets moved in orbits around the sun.

C. Nicholas Copernicus, a Polish priest, proposed a model in 1514.

D. There are many popular theories about the solar system. Ancient People believed that the sun moved around the earth and the earth was static.
solution:
The correct answer is **"DCBA".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement D** is the opening sentence of the passage which explains **the theories available and what ancient people believed about the movement of the Sun and the Earth.**
 
• **Statement C** is the second sentence of the passage which introduces **Nicholas Copernicus and his proposed model and which year it was proposed.** 
 
• **Statement B** is the third sentence of the passage which explains the **theory of Nicholas Copernicus**.
 
• **Statement A** is the last sentence of the passage which shows that **other astronomers like,** **Johannes Kepler and Galileo supported the Copernican theory after nearly a century passed.​**
 
• Hence, the correct sequence is **D, C, B, A.**

 

**The correct passage is:** ***D.** There are many popular theories about the solar system. Ancient People believed that the sun moved around the earth and the earth was static. **C.** Nicholas Copernicus, a Polish priest, proposed a model in 1514. **B.** Copernicus’ view was that the sun was stationary and the earth and the planets moved in orbits around the sun. **A.** Two astronomers – Johannes Kepler from Germany and Galileo from Italy – supported the Copernican theory after nearly a century passed by.*
